subject: Core Mathematics
substrand: Surface Area and Volume of Solids

conflicts.fact: Surface area of the rectangular box and what it means for the cylindrical drum's 'same sheet'
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 computes the box (120×80×100 cm) as 59,200 cm². Check: 2(9600+12000+8000)=59,200, which is correct. Lessons 6 and 7 then state the drum also has 59,200 cm² with height 100 cm. Lesson 6 back-calculates r ≈ 59.2 cm, but 2πr²+2πr(100)=59,200 gives r≈ 59.2 only if the formula is mis-solved. For r=59.2 cm, SA≈ 22,000+37,200=59,200, so it is consistent. Lesson 7 states 59,200 cm² = 5.92 m², but 59,200 cm² is 5.92 m², so that is fine. The conflict is the box volume: 120×80×100 = 960,000 cm³ = 0.96 m³, consistent.

conflicts.fact: Drum volume and difference vs box
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 Learned/Overview say the drum's volume is ≈1,100,000 cm³ (1.10 m³), about 15% more than the box's 960,000 cm³. Lesson 6 Explained says the drum holds about 140,000 cm³ (140 litres) more, but π(59.2)²(100) ≈ 1,101,000 cm³, so the difference is ~141,000 cm³. These are consistent, though the 15% figure is approximate. The real conflict is the radius: with r=59.2 cm the drum is 118 cm wide and 100 cm tall, while the box is only 120×80×100 cm, which is fine.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbering/scope of surface-area and volume coverage
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says volumes for cylinders/cuboids come in Lessons 4–5, and that volume calculations in Lessons 4–5 complete the explanation. Lesson 4 is actually surface area of spheres and composites, and Lesson 5 says the cylinder volume formula comes in Lesson 6. Lesson 6 also says Lesson 7 is composite solids and optimisation, while Lesson 4 already covered composite surface area.

conflicts.fact: Cylinder volume treatment and Lesson 5 volume stated as predicted vs established
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 predicts the drum holds more because circular cross-section is more efficient. Lesson 6 says cylinder volume formula is not yet known and uses V_cone = ⅓V_cylinder, while computing the drum volume; Lesson 6 never derives V = πr²h, whereas Lesson 5 says it will be derived in Lesson 6.

conflicts.fact: Name of the posho mill owner/metalsmith
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 and 6 name the mill owner Mama Wanjiru; Lesson 6 also calls the metalsmith Mwangi; Lesson 8 says Mwangi the metalsmith cut the sheet, and Lesson 7 says her cylindrical drum. Lesson 7 names the water tank owner Mwangi wa Kamau, and Lesson 7's silo farmer is Mwalimu Chebet.

conflicts.fact: Composite solid example locations and dimensions
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 describes a Mombasa water tank (cylinder + hemisphere) and a Nakuru silo with radius 1.4 m, height 3 m, slant height 2 m. Lesson 7 describes the cylinder+hemisphere tank in Makueni (Mwangi wa Kamau) and the silo in Eldoret (Mwalimu Chebet) with radius 1.2 m, height 3.5 m, cone height 0.9 m, while its Observed section calls it the Nakuru grain silo.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 4 says the gas cylinder has two hemispheres, and Lesson 8 says the cylinder beats a same-height box
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 Overview uses a gas cylinder (cylinder + two hemispheres), but Learned/Observed list a Mombasa water tank (cylinder + hemisphere). Lesson 8 states the cylinder consistently wins versus a same-height rectangular prism, while Lesson 4's DQB suggests a sphere would hold more for the same surface area, which is unmentioned in the isoperimetric claim 'among solids' that the cylinder is best.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons the prediction refers to
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 says 'seven lessons' of study, and the sequence indeed has 8 lessons; Lesson 3 says 'Lesson 3 of 8' while Lesson 6 calls itself the resolution lesson of an eight-lesson sequence, yet Lesson 8 then resolves the driving question again as a final explanation.
